subject: Observability evidence, synthetic probing plan and measurement definitions
messages:
From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@globex.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@globex.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: measurement protocol and evidence for uptime/latency SLOs

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for taking this RFP. As part of our security and procurement review we need a detailed description of how Redwood defines, measures, and reports uptime and latency for inference endpoints. Specifically:

- Precise measurement windows (UTC) and sampling cadence.
- Exact definitions for "eligible requests" vs. trimmed/ignored traffic.
- The telemetry used for p95/p99 latency (client RTT vs. server-side inference time vs. end-to-end).
- Synthetic probing methodology (who runs probes, where, cadence, how probes are excluded from billing/SLAs).
- Service credit calculation examples for outages and latency degradations.
- Evidence packaging requirements (logs, traces, synthetic probe history, hash of sampling script), and format for delivery during audits.

Can you send a proposal and a short matrix that maps measurement artifacts to auditable evidence? We have a security review meeting on Friday and would like your draft before then.

Thanks,
Dana
Procurement Lead, Globex Inc.
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@globex.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: measurement protocol and evidence for uptime/latency SLOs

Hi Dana —

Appreciate the clear list. Attaching an initial proposal (Redwood-SLA-Measurement-Proposal-v1.pdf) and our synthetic probing plan (Synthetic-Probing-Plan.xlsx). High-level answers inline; detailed artifacts attached.

Quick summary:
- Measurement windows: 5-minute aligned samples aggregated into daily windows (UTC). We provide per-route and per-model aggregation.
- Eligibility: "Eligible requests" are customer-originated inference API calls that successfully reach our ingress and are not administratively excluded (e.g., known test probes if opted-in to exclude). Retries due to client error (4xx) are excluded.
- Latency signal: reported p50/p90/p95/p99 are computed from server-side request completion timestamps (time request dequeued to token-generation-complete), with optional end-to-end measurement if customers install our small client SDK.
- Synthetic probes: we run distributed probes from three regions by default; customers can opt for private probes. Probes are tagged and excluded from billing/SLAs; we provide full probe history and hashes of probe scripts for audits.
- Credits: sample credit matrix included in the PDF (examples).

Hannah, Karthik, Priyom — can you review the measurement exclusions and the credit examples; need any changes before I send to Dana and the procurement team.

Sofia
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood-SLA-Measurement-Proposal-v1.pdf (18 pages)
Attachment: Synthetic-Probing-Plan.xlsx (workbook)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: RFI: measurement protocol and evidence for uptime/latency SLOs

Sofia — quick notes from SRE perspective:

1) Sampling windows: 1-min internal buckets, aggregated to 5-min aligned samples for public telemetry. That keeps the math simple for NTP drift and clock skew.

2) Eligibility edge cases: we should explicitly call out maintenance-mode failovers and multi-tenant throttles. Proposed language: "Requests impacted by planned maintenance windows that were announced >=72 hours in advance and routed to maintenance targets are excluded from SLA calculations."

3) Latency signal nuance: our server-side measurement uses request-entered-execution to request-complete (this excludes queue wait if running on reserved pools with pre-warming disabled). For Hosted API customers queue wait is included; for Dedicated customers we can agree to exclude queueing if they use guaranteed capacity. We should give both options in the doc.

4) Synthetic probe cadence: default 10m per region; increase to 1m under outage investigation. Probes are labelled with probe-id and hash; we store raw probe traces for 365 days for enterprise customers.

I'll add a short appendix describing how the telemetry maps to trace IDs and the runbook for incident attribution.

-hannah
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Team —

Thanks Hannah — those options look good. A few commercial notes before Sofia replies to procurement:

- Credit matrix: propose we keep three tiers (Minor latency degradation, Partial outage, Major outage) with credits expressed as % of monthly invoice. Examples in the attached PDF. We should be prepared to show a worked example for a 30-day billing period.
- Measurement transparency: procurement will ask for anonymized samples of the raw telemetry. We should offer a redacted package (trace IDs, timestamps, p95/p99 windows) as a sample audit bundle.
- Roll-forward clause: include language that we may update sampling cadence or probe locations with 30 days notice, and provide a changelog.

If no objections I'll sign off on the draft and Sofia can send it to Dana.

-karthik

Dana —

Thanks — please find attached our requested artifacts: Redwood-SLA-Measurement-Proposal-v1.pdf and Synthetic-Probing-Plan.xlsx. Key operational commitments (executive summary):

1) Uptime definition and measurement
- Uptime % is measured per 30-day billing period as: 1 - (sum of eligible outage seconds / total eligible seconds in period). Eligible outage seconds are periods where our routing layer returns 5xx errors or where inference requests exceed the configured failure threshold for a route.
- We compute this from server-side telemetry (ingress accepted timestamp to final response status). We retain raw telemetry for 365 days; summary metrics for 540 days.

2) Latency definition
- Default latency SLOs reported as p95 and p99 using server-side completion times (start of token generation to end-of-generation). For Hosted customers we include queue wait; for Dedicated customers we can optionally exclude queue wait if guaranteed capacity is purchased.
- Example: p95 <= 250ms for the route example in PDF, p99 <= 450ms. These are configurable per-route in contract.

3) Synthetic probing and exclusion
- Default probe cadence: 10 minutes per region (US/ EU/ APAC); customers may request private probe endpoints. Probes are flagged and excluded from SLA/billing; probe logs and script hashes are included in audit bundles.

4) Evidence and audit bundle
- We will provide (a) daily summary CSV (p50/p90/p95/p99 + uptime sample), (b) redacted raw telemetry sample (trace IDs + timestamps), (c) synthetic probe history CSV, (d) runbook excerpts for incident attribution. Templates are in the attached PDF.

5) Credit matrix (examples) — summarized from the PDF
- Uptime >= 99.99%: no credit
- 99.95% <= Uptime < 99.99%: 5% credit of monthly bill for affected services
- 99.5% <= Uptime < 99.95%: 15% credit
- Uptime < 99.5%: 30% credit + executive review

We can adjust thresholds for enterprise deals; the attached proposal contains worked numeric examples for a 30-day billing cycle and sample calculation scripts. If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with SRE this week.

Sofia
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
